question: Who helped their teammates more in 2015-16, Curry or LeBron?
answer:
# On-Court Impact Review

## Answer

**My judgement: I lean toward Stephen Curry.**

**Criterion:** Evaluating playmaking and team on-minus-off impact in the 2015-16 regular season.

**Decisive reason:** Using the regular season as the primary phase, Stephen Curry recorded higher assists per 36 minutes and a stronger on-minus-off net rating compared to LeBron James. Stephen Curry helped his team achieve a larger positive scoring margin when on the court versus the bench. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612744&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Regular+Season&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612739&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Regular+Season&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=)

**Strongest counterargument:** LeBron James generated more assists per 36 minutes, a higher assists per turnover ratio, and a much higher on-minus-off net rating during the playoffs. However, following the priority policy, the regular season serves as the primary phase for a season-long question. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612744&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Playoffs&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612739&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Playoffs&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=)

**Why this judgement:** Stephen Curry provided higher raw assist volume per 36 minutes in the regular season, while LeBron James maintained a slightly better assists per turnover ratio during that same phase.

**What could change it:** Shifting priority entirely to the playoff phase or emphasizing ball security over assist volume would reverse the preference to LeBron James.

## Dimension findings

- **Playmaking and ball security:** The indicators disagree; one player does not dominate all selected measures.
- **Team on/off context:** Regular Season: Stephen Curry has the higher on-minus-off net rating; Playoffs: LeBron James has the higher on-minus-off net rating. This describes team association, not an isolated player effect.

This position compares observed contributions, not innate ability. Playmaking uses assists per minute and assists/turnovers, not a complete model of creation. Team on/off is association rather than causation.

**Scope:** 2015-16–2015-16 versus 2015-16–2015-16; Regular Season, Playoffs.

- **Playmaking and ball security / Regular Season:** Stephen Curry (2015): Assists per 36 minutes **7.03** per 36 minutes, Assists per turnover **2.01** ratio; LeBron James (2015): Assists per 36 minutes **6.83** per 36 minutes, Assists per turnover **2.06** ratio. - **Team on/off context / Regular Season:** Stephen Curry (2015 / Golden State Warriors): On-minus-off net rating **23.1** points / 100 possessions, ON min **2,700** minutes, OFF min **1,276** minutes; LeBron James (2015 / Cleveland Cavaliers): On-minus-off net rating **16.1** points / 100 possessions, ON min **2,709** minutes, OFF min **1,262** minutes.
